column1: # parse-time sugar and nothing else. `x |> f(a)` IS `f(x, a)` — the
# piped value goes in as the FIRST argument, because every Aontu call is
# data-first already and a pipe must read the way the calls it replaces
# EVERY CANON ROW HERE SHOWS A CALL, never the token: by the time a Val
# exists the pipe is gone, which is what keeps canon — and the two
# ports' agreement about it — untouched by this phase.
# The right-hand side is a call, or the bare NAME of one. A constraint
# atom that BUILT is neither: an atom with its argument list complete is
# a residual rather than a call waiting for a subject, and `1 |>
# neq(2,3)` is asking for `1 & neq(2,3)`, which is what `&` is for.
# A call written with SEVERAL arguments still takes the piped value on
# already has its argument is a call the pipe would over-fill, which
# A call the arity check REFUSED, whose piped form satisfies it: the
# comma group the author wrote is reopened and the piped value joins
# A call that could not be BUILT — its target is not a function name —
# is already refused when the pipe sees it, and keeps its own code:
# `pipe_target` would say "the right-hand side is not a call", where
# the truth is that it is a call spelling with no function to call.
# TypeScript keeps unknown_function through the pipe; so does Go.
